newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Vice-Premier Wu Bangguo said Sino-U.S. relations had improved recently, with an increased number of bilateral visits and discussions.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Public response towards the nomination of candidates for Hong Kong's provisional legislature was active. Several members of the present Legislative Council collected application forms.
-- Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen told Hong Kong bankers that Hong Kong's financial system will remain unchanged after the territory's handover to Chinese sovereignty next year.

-- MING PAO -- Members of the Selection Committee nominated each other for seats on the provisional legislature, while political parties traded votes. One the first day of the nomination process, 57 collected application forms.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- A pro-Beijing analyst said any candidate who collects 120 votes will have a place in the provisional legislature, which made it easy for major forces to control the selection of the council.
-- APPLE DAILY -- Many politicians who were defeated in last year's Legistative Council elections plan to make a comeback in the provisional legislature selection.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- The China Securities Regulatory Commission was considering opening the mainland market to Hong Kong securities dealers after the yuan becomes convertible. Some local securities companies are considering opening branches in China.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- MasterCard will acquire a 51 per cent stake in London-based Mondex International and use Mondex's technology to develop its future products.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- China is to offer foreign retailers unprecedented access to its potentially huge market in a bid to speed up its accession to the World Trade Organisation.
-- China said it would reduce grain imports by more than half of last year's volume to seven million tonnes this year.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- An American expert said China must push ahead with developing its eonomic institutions before it can move up the ladder of world competitiveness.
-- A European Union vice-president said Beijing was moving closer to liberalising its insurance sector and to allowing foreign participation in broadcasting and telecommunications.
